name: Mariam Gviniashvili
description: Interference is a performance in two movements: a live spatial audio followed by an audiovisual set.Here, glitches and interruptions are not treated as accidents; they are the architecture. The work explores the friction between signal and noise, focusing on the atmosphere of interference rather than discrete events. It is a study of the threshold where order and disturbance become indistinguishable. What appears as chaos at one scale is revealed as a pattern at another - a behaviour born from the interaction of broken fragments.
bio: Mariam Gviniashvili is a composer, sound artist, and visual artist working at the intersection of electroacoustic music, 3D sound, and instrumental composition. Her work explores the emotional and spatial dimensions of sound, often in close relation to visual media. Originally from Georgia, Mariam began her artistic journey as a singer and pianist before studying composition in Tbilisi, Budapest, and Oslo. This diverse background informs projects such as Trails and Deconstruction, both awarded Honorary Mentions by Prix Ars Electronica (Austria), or Ruins, winner of the 40.4 Festival for Ambisonic Works (USA) and The Work of the Year (Norway). Mariam has been commissioned by INA GRM, ZKM | Center for Art and Media, Notam, Henie Onstad Art Centre, MA/IN Festival, and the Hong Kong Visualisation Research Centre. Her work has been presented internationally at ZKM, Ars Electronica, EMPAC, Virginia Tech, CCRMA, BEASTFEaST, Ultima Festival, and has been broadcast on BBC, SWR and NRK radio.
